title: Change of Conditions
sub: Lift the NRPF condition, free
cells:
What you get

Opens public funds

Time to apply

2 to 4 hours, mostly gathering statements

Decision: 34 days on Home Office figures, up to 93 days on independent analysis
docs: Bank statements for EVERY account you hold, most recent 6 months
Proof of income and all outgoings
Evidence of your accommodation and any rent arrears
For the child-welfare ground: evidence about your children
steps:
Step 1:
Check your route qualifies: family, private life or BN(O). Work and study routes only in particularly compelling circumstances.

Step 2:
Pick your ground: you are destitute, at risk of destitution within 3 months, there are compelling child-welfare reasons, or exceptional financial circumstances.

Step 3:
Download the change of conditions form from GOV.UK and complete it in full.

Step 4:
Disclose every bank account you hold. Missing one is the most common reason for refusal.

Step 5:
Attach a short covering letter explaining your situation in plain terms and listing your evidence.

Step 6:
Submit online and keep the confirmation.
rules: Family, private life or BN(O) route (work/study only in particularly compelling circumstances)
Destitute, at risk within 3 months, child welfare, or exceptional circumstances

title: Visa fee waiver
sub: Extension fees waived
cells:
Could be worth

£3,900

Saved per adult per cycle

Time to apply

2 to 3 hours

Decision: Historically 69 to 168 days
docs: 6 months of bank statements for every account
Payslips or proof of any income
Details of anyone supporting you financially
steps:
Step 1:
Confirm your route: family (5 or 10 year), private life, discretionary leave, BN(O) or trafficking victim.

Step 2:
Complete the fee waiver request as part of your extension application on GOV.UK.

Step 3:
Set out your income, then your essential living costs, and show what is left.

Step 4:
Upload 6 months of statements for every account.

Step 5:
Submit BEFORE your current leave expires so section 3C protection continues.

title: National Insurance number
sub: Free, opens everything contributory
cells:
Time to apply

About 15 minutes

Decision: Up to 4 weeks
docs: Your passport or eVisa share code
steps:
Step 1:
Check your BRP first: some already show a National Insurance number, in which case you do not need to apply.

Step 2:
Apply on GOV.UK. It is online only.

Step 3:
Upload identity evidence when asked.

Step 4:
Wait for the letter. You can start work before it arrives using your eVisa share code.
rules: Living in the UK with the right to work
fund: Not a public fund. Your visa condition does not apply.
what: Free, online only. Makes work clean, builds contributory entitlement, and is required for childcare accounts, student finance and LISAs.
valueNote: About the amount: builds New Style JSA/ESA and State Pension entitlement; needed for childcare accounts and LISA.
boost: Give an address where post reliably reaches you, and tell them promptly if you move.
Start work without waiting: your employer can use a temporary reference.
watch: Paying a third-party website. The application is free on GOV.UK and no one can speed it up for money.

title: GP registration
sub: Free NHS primary care
cells:
Time to apply

15 minutes

Decision: Usually same day to 2 weeks
docNone: Nothing is legally required
steps:
Step 1:
Find a practice near you on the NHS website.

Step 2:
Ask to register. Fill in form GMS1 at reception or online.

Step 3:
If you have no proof of address or ID, say so and ask to register anyway: NHS policy allows it.

Step 4:
If you are homeless, you may use the surgery address.
rules: Live in or near the practice area
No ID, proof of address or immigration status required (NHS policy)
fund: Not a public fund. Your visa condition does not apply.
what: Free primary care and the gateway to all NHS services. No ID, no proof of address, no immigration status required (NHS policy). Homeless patients can use the surgery's address.
valueNote: About the amount: gateway to all NHS services.
boost: If you are turned away, ask for the refusal in writing with the reason. Practices can only refuse if the list is closed or you are outside the area.
Register before you are ill: it is the gateway to nearly everything else in the NHS.
watch: Accepting "we need ID and proof of address" as final. It is not a legal requirement.

valueNote: About the amount: scales with band; exemption also covers a student's non-working non-British spouse or dependant.
boost: The exemption also covers the non-British spouse or dependant of a full-time student who cannot work or claim under their visa: include them and send their share code.
Always ask for backdating. Councils do backdate with evidence, and that can be a year or more of bills.
You need a course of 1 year or more, and 21+ study hours a week.
watch: Do not confuse this with Council Tax Reduction, which is a public fund and blocked under NRPF. This exemption is based on who lives in the property, not income, so it is NRPF-safe.

docs: Student certificate from your university (free, ask the registry)
Share code for a non-working spouse or dependant
steps: Get a council tax student certificate from your university: it is free and usually instant online.
Find your council's council tax discount page.
Apply for the Class N student exemption. If everyone in the household is a student, the bill is zero.
Upload the certificate and your tenancy.
Ask for it to be backdated to your course or tenancy start date.
rules: Full-time course, 1 year+ and 21+ hours a week
expect.about: Composition-based, not means-tested, so NRPF-safe: full-time student exemption (Class N, all-student household pays nothing, and it covers the student's non-working non-British spouse or dependant), 25% single person discount, 50% all-disregarded. Never confuse with Council Tax Reduction, which is a public fund.
expect.nrpfNote: discounts and exemptions are not public funds; never confuse with Council Tax Reduction which is
expect.valueNote: scales with band; exemption also covers a student's non-working non-British spouse or dependant
boost: The exemption also covers the non-British spouse or dependant of a full-time student who cannot work or claim under their visa: include them and send their share code.
Always ask for backdating. Councils do backdate with evidence, and that can be a year or more of bills.
You need a course of 1 year or more, and 21+ study hours a week.
expect.strengthen: Ask for backdating to course or tenancy start
expect.watch: Do not confuse this with Council Tax Reduction, which is a public fund and blocked under NRPF. This exemption is based on who lives in the property, not income, so it is NRPF-safe.

One phone call

docs: Referral voucher from a partner agency (Citizens Advice, school, GP, council)
steps:
Step 1:
Ring Help through Hardship free on 0808 208 2138: it is the fastest route to a voucher.

Step 2:
Or ask any of these for a referral: Citizens Advice, your GP, your child's school, a social worker, the council.

Step 3:
Take the voucher to the food bank at its opening time.

Step 4:
You receive at least 3 days of emergency food.

fund: Not a public fund. Your visa condition does not apply.

valueNote: About the amount: no immigration check; community fridges and baby banks need no referral at all.
boost: The Help through Hardship line also checks what else you are missing and can refer you onward: it is worth the call even if you already have a voucher.
Ask for a fuel voucher at the same appointment: many food banks issue Fuel Bank Foundation vouchers.
Independent food banks (774 of them) often accept self-referral with no voucher at all.
watch: Nothing: there is no immigration check anywhere in this system.

sub: Free insulation and heating
cells:
What you get

Free home upgrades

30 minutes to register interest

steps:
Step 1:
Check your council's Warm Homes or ECO4 LA Flex pages.

Step 2:
Register interest: qualifying routes include income around £36,000 or less, an eligible postcode, or a cold-related health condition.

A surveyor assesses the property.

Work is installed free: insulation, heating upgrades, or a £7,500 heat pump grant through the Boiler Upgrade Scheme.
rules: EPC D-G home (owner) or E-G (rented, landlord consent)

fund: It depends on your situation.
what: The £15bn ECO successor (from January 2026). Boiler Upgrade Scheme: £7,500 heat pump grant.
valueNote: About the amount: Boiler Upgrade Scheme: £7,500 heat pump grant.
boost: The income and postcode routes need no benefit at all, which is what makes them work for NRPF households.

watch: Never pay an agent to "arrange" a grant. Councils and accredited installers do it free.

Step 1:
Pick one of the nine designated banks, or try Monzo or Starling which open accounts in-app.

Say clearly that you want a BASIC BANK ACCOUNT: it is fee-free, has a debit card, and has no credit check barrier.

fund: Not a public fund. Your visa condition does not apply.

valueNote: About the amount: nine designated banks must offer them; eVisa share code or any-country passport works; Monzo/Starling flexible on address proof.
boost: Ask for the "basic bank account" by name. Branch staff often steer people to standard accounts that they then fail the checks for.

steps: Complete the ASF1 form with help from a support organisation such as Migrant Help.
Ring Migrant Help free on 0808 8010 503: they complete it with you.
Submit with evidence of destitution.
Support is paid onto an ARC card, with accommodation if you need it.
expect.about: The parallel system for asylum seekers: £49.18 per person per week self-catered on the Aspen card (£9.95 catered) plus £5.25 pregnancy, £9.50 baby under 1, £5.25 child 1-3, one-off £300 maternity payment, plus accommodation. Became a discretionary power on 2 June 2026 (refusable for late claims, illegal working, manufactured destitution; tribunal appeal rights remain, ASAP represents free). Work ban 12 months, then permitted work restricted to RQF 6+ roles (widened 27 March 2026). Section 4: same card rate for refused claims meeting narrow conditions, no cash. Ends 42 days after a positive decision.
expect.nrpfNote: not a public fund; became a discretionary power on 2 June 2026 (refusable for late claims, illegal working, manufactured destitution)
expect.valueNote: £49.18/week self-catered on the Aspen card + pregnancy/child supplements + £300 maternity one-off; plus accommodation; ends 42 days after a positive decision
boost: Ask about section 98 emergency support while the section 95 decision is pending: you should not be left with nothing.
Your ARC card opens other things: free NHS prescriptions via HC2, Scotland's free bus travel, and many food banks and charities.
Ask for a maternity payment if you are pregnant.
expect.strengthen: ASAP represents free at the support tribunal
expect.watch: Do not wait until you are completely without money. Applying takes time and section 98 exists to bridge the gap.
